name: Delaware
nameStory: Follow the chain backwards: the state is named for the Delaware River, which is named for Thomas West, Baron De La Warr, a governor of Virginia who never set foot in it. Colonists then pinned that same dead baron's name onto the Lenape people, who called themselves something else entirely.
capitalStory: William Penn put Dover inland on purpose. A capital on the coast could be shelled or raided from the sea, so he placed the seat of government safely in the middle of the colony.

majorFeatures.name: Delaware River
majorFeatures.note: The northern border and port route

majorFeatures.name: Atlantic Coastal Plain
majorFeatures.note: Flat sandy lowland covering the state

funFacts: First to ratify the Constitution, on December 7, 1787, which is the whole reason for 'The First State.'
More than half of all publicly traded US companies are legally incorporated in Delaware, for its specialized business court.
Its highest point is about 448 feet, the lowest 'highest point' of any state.
Delaware's northern border is a perfect arc: the Twelve-Mile Circle, the only circular state boundary in America.
